{{recipe}}

'''Khanom mo keang''' (Thai: ขนมหม้อแกง), or '''khanom khumpamas''' (Thai: ขนมกุมภมาศ) is a Thai [[Cookbook:Custard|custard]] dessert. In present-day Thailand, the dessert is prepared in a square aluminum pan.

== History ==
Khanom Mo Keang was created by Maria Guyomar de Pinha (Thao Thong Kip Ma), a Japanese-Portuguese woman who made the dessert in the Ayutthaya royal court kitchen. She adapted Western custard to Thai cuisine by substituting several locally-available ingredients for those traditionally used in the West. She substituted duck eggs for chicken eggs, coconut milk for cow milk/cream, and palm/coconut sugar for cane sugar. This took place during the reign of King Narai the Great in the 17th century.

== Ingredients ==

* 1 large [[Cookbook:Shallot|shallot]], peeled and thinly [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
* ⅓ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]
* 1 cup (236 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Coconut Sugar|coconut]] or [[Cookbook:Palm Sugar|palm sugar]]
* 1½ cups (300 g) cooked and hulled [[Cookbook:Mung Bean|mung beans]]
* 4 large whole chicken [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]] plus 3 [[Cookbook:Egg Yolk|yolks]] (or 5 duck eggs)
* ⅔ cup (144 g) [[Cookbook:Granulated Sugar|granulated sugar]]
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Coconut Cream|coconut cream]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]

== Procedure ==

# Put the shallot slices and oil into a small [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] over medium-low heat. Stir the shallot slices, until they are golden brown and crispy.
# Grease the bottom and sides of a 9×13-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] [[Cookbook:Baking Pan|baking pan]]. Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 180°C.
# Soften the palm or coconut sugar in a pan over medium heat.
# [[Cookbook:Puréeing|Blend]] the mung beans, eggs, both sugars, coconut cream, salt, and any leftover oil from the shallots together until smooth.
# Let the custard mixture sit for 5 minutes until it becomes less frothy.
# Pour the custard mixture into the pan. Place the pan on a rack positioned in the upper third of the oven. [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] at 180°C for 35–45 minutes or until the center is slightly firm and the top is golden brown.
# Put some of the fried shallots over the top of the custard.
